courseTitle: Learn the Basics of React Native
description: Learn the core fundamentals of React Native: native components (View, Text, Image), JSX syntax, Components, Props and State.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.description: React Native is like React, but it uses native components instead of web components. To understand React Native, you must learn JSX, components, props, and state.
keyPoints: Works for beginners and React developers

sections.title: Hello World
sections.description: The first React Native app displays a simple 'Hello World' text using core components.

sections.title: Core Components
sections.description: React Native provides core components that map to native UI elements.

components.name: View
components.purpose: Acts as a container like div

sections.title: JSX and ES6
sections.description: JSX allows writing UI code inside JavaScript. React Native supports ES6 features out of the box.

sections.title: Components
sections.description: Everything visible on the screen in React Native is a component.

sections.title: Props
sections.description: Props are read-only values passed from parent to child components.

sections.title: State
sections.description: State allows components to change data over time in response to user actions.

sections.title: React vs React Native State
sections.description: State management is the same in React and React Native using hooks or class components.

code.example:
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);

<Button title="Click me" onPress={() => setCount(count + 1)} />
